strengths: Identifies a novel, important, and practically consequential phenomenon: narrow finetuning leaves strong, easily-detectable traces in early-token activation differences, with direct implications for the validity of widely-used 'model organism' methodology in AI safety/interpretability research.

Very extensive empirical coverage: 33 organisms spanning 4 distinct families (SDF, emergent misalignment, subliminal learning, taboo word games) across 7 models from 1B to 32B parameters and 3 model families (Gemma, Llama, Qwen), plus an additional vision-language domain-adaptation generalization check.

Methodologically creative and rigorous evaluation: builds an LLM-based interpretability agent with a fixed interaction budget and reproducible grading rubrics per organism type, providing a quantitative, less subjective way to validate that ADL signals carry real information (rather than relying only on qualitative researcher inspection).

Goes beyond mere observation to provide a causal explanation (projection-based ablation showing the bias helps finetuning-data loss and hurts pretraining-data loss) supporting the overfitting/catastrophic-forgetting hypothesis, and tests a concrete mitigation (mixing pretraining data) with honest reporting of its trade-offs (reduced false-fact internalization).

Substantial robustness/ablation work: positional analysis, full vs LoRA finetuning, base-vs-chat-model comparisons, comparison against CAFT-based concept ablation, different agent backbones (GPT-5, GPT-5-chat, Gemini 2.5 Pro), and a Bayesian hierarchical GLM to statistically support the main claims.
High transparency and reproducibility effort: detailed appendix with exact prompts, grading rubrics, hyperparameters for Patchscope/steering calibration, and organism descriptions.
weaknesses: Heavy reliance on LLM-based graders/judges at nearly every stage (token relevance, coherence checking, hypothesis grading, Patchscope scale selection) introduces potential circularity and systematic bias that is only partially addressed by variance/robustness checks; the paper's own limitations section acknowledges this but does not fully resolve it.

The generalization test to more realistic domain-specific (vision-language) finetuning shows the effect is 'almost entirely absent,' which somewhat undercuts the strength of the paper's broader claims about narrow finetuning in general versus the specific synthetic/narrow organisms studied, and the agent's inability to send images is a confound in that experiment.

The proposed mitigation (mixing in pretraining/unrelated data) reduces detectability but also degrades the model's internalization of the target objective (lower FFA scores), so it is not clear this constitutes a fully satisfying solution for model-organism design going forward.

Some conflation between 'narrowness of finetuning objective' and 'semantic homogeneity of the finetuning corpus' as the root cause is not fully disentangled experimentally (e.g., whether topical diversity vs. task narrowness is the operative variable).

Reproducibility artifact section is incomplete in the provided manuscript (code availability link is blank), and some organism categories rely on very few instances (e.g., only one subliminal-learning organism), limiting statistical robustness of conclusions for that category.

Grading rubrics and agent system prompts were authored by the same team designing the method, which could introduce subtle experimenter bias in what counts as a 'successful' identification, despite efforts to keep the agent blind to the true objective.
